questions.q: What does DORA stand for, and what did its research produce?
options: DevOps Research and Assessment; four metrics that separate high-performing software teams from the rest
Database Operations Reliability Audit; a checklist for database backups
Deployment Oversight and Risk Analysis; a risk-scoring algorithm
Developer Onboarding and Retention Analytics; a hiring metric
questions.explain: DORA (DevOps Research and Assessment) is the research program that studied thousands of organizations and identified four key metrics correlated with high software delivery performance.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the four DORA metrics?
options: Lines of code written per developer per day
Number of meetings held per sprint
Lead Time for Changes
Total number of GitHub stars
questions.explain: Lead Time for Changes — the time from a commit landing on main to that commit running in production — is one of the four DORA metrics, alongside Deployment Frequency, Change Failure Rate, and Time to Restore Service.

questions.q: How does DORA group its four metrics into two pairs?
options: Throughput (Deployment Frequency, Lead Time for Changes) and Stability (Change Failure Rate, Time to Restore Service)
Cost and Revenue
Frontend and Backend metrics
Manual and Automated metrics
questions.explain: DORA groups the metrics into throughput (how fast: Deployment Frequency and Lead Time for Changes) and stability (how safe: Change Failure Rate and Time to Restore Service).

questions.q: What is DORA's key counterintuitive finding about speed and stability?
options: Teams must always sacrifice speed for stability
Teams must always sacrifice stability for speed
Speed and stability are not a trade-off — elite teams achieve both at the same time
Speed and stability are unrelated and cannot both be measured
questions.explain: DORA's research found that high-performing teams are both fast and stable simultaneously, because practices like small changes and automated testing improve both at once rather than trading one for the other.

questions.q: In the Northbridge Retail example, what does a 5% Change Failure Rate mean?
options: 5% of all code written contains bugs
2 out of the last 40 releases caused a production failure
The team deploys only 5% as often as competitors
5% of customers reported a problem with the app
questions.explain: Change Failure Rate is the percentage of deployments that cause a failure in production. In the example, 2 bad releases out of the last 40 deployments works out to a 5% change failure rate, which is in the elite range.
